title: Add text strings for H.281 directions

notes.body:
I can't see failed pipeline, but I think its tools/check_tfs.py complaining:


Error: epan/dissectors/packet-h224.c tilt_direction - could have used tfs_up_down from tfs.c instead:  {"Up", "Down"}
and also in / out (and right left ?)

Nope, neither are in tfs.c

Running check_tfs.py with --common shows that there are still only 3 pairs (not in tfs.c) that appear 3 times:

('FFD', 'RFD') appears 3 times, in:  ['epan/dissectors/packet-ieee802154.c', 'epan/dissectors/packet-mle.c', 'epan/dissectors/packet-zbncp.c']

('Data PDU', 'Control PDU') appears 3 times, in:  ['epan/dissectors/packet-pdcp-lte.c', 'epan/dissectors/packet-pdcp-nr.c', 'epan/dissectors/packet-rlc-nr.c']

('Message sent to originating side', 'Message sent from originating side') appears 3 times, in:  ['epan/dissectors/packet-q2931.c', 'epan/dissectors/packet-q931.c', 'epan/dissectors/packet-q933.c']


These could be added to tfs.c...  I am tempted to add an option to show how many times each of the tfs values tfs.c are referenced (by counting dissectors' object files that reference them like check_static.py does).  I wonder if they are even all in use?
Should i add new tfs definitions to tfs.c? I wanted to do this, but the potential for these definitions to be used elsewhere seems unlikely to me.
They are very basic names/opposites, but I think its reasonable to wait until there are a few usages (check_tfs.py --common mentions if > 2) before adding to tfs.c

```
/home/user/ws/wireshark/epan# for i in $(cat tfs.h | grep "tfs_" | awk '{print $4}' | cut -d ";" -f 1); do grep -r "$i" ./dissectors/ | echo "$i : $(wc -l)"; done | grep "^tfs.* : 0$"
tfs_ack_nack : 0
tfs_allow_block : 0
tfs_restricted_allowed : 0
tfs_accept_reject : 0
tfs_found_not_found : 0
tfs_registered_not_registered : 0
tfs_provisioned_not_provisioned : 0
tfs_c2s_s2c : 0
```

It doesn't surprise me that there are some entries in tfs.h/c that are not actually used, but I would have guessed that some of these would be fairly common!  I wouldn't object to deleting them - the only hesitation is that someone may be using them in private dissectors (plugins can't link them on Windows).

Adding lots of entries that are only single-use will make this file unwieldly.  I don't feel strongly about it, but personally I'd prefer to add right_left and in_out locally to this file.  If other dissectors also need them, tools/check_tfs.py --common will notice and they can be added then.
